basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 10.' and it opens '| Vers. 10. Quam cum vidisset Jacob, et sciret consobrinam suam. Quaeri potest unde'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 10. Quam cum vidisset Jacob, et sciret consobrinam suam. Quaeri potest unde nosset eam consobrinam suam esse, quam nunquam ante viderat? Sed scire possumus hoc eum a pastoribus didicisse, cum quibus antea locutus fuerat. Ideoque mox ut eam vidit, cum fiducia in ejus osculum irruit.
